Internal helper: a radix order for text, whatever its encoding mark

Source: R/utils.R
dot-jst_text_order.Rd

Session 390 (the non-English probe): R's radix sort refuses a vector whose first non-missing string is not ASCII and carries no encoding mark ("Character encoding must be UTF-8, Latin-1 or bytes"), on every platform, and text read from a CSV file – by jload() or read.csv() – or typed into a script that is source()d carries none. jencode() on a CSV variable whose first word was Zurich spelled with its umlaut, or a word in Chinese, stopped in R's words. Each character key is given its UTF-8 mark first (enc2utf8(), which in a UTF-8 session only marks the text), so the order is the radix order of the same bytes.

Usage

.jst_text_order(..., decreasing = FALSE)

Arguments

...

The keys, as order() takes them.

decreasing

As order()'s.

Value

Integer permutation, as order(..., method = "radix").
